 Judgment
Petitioner has filed this petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation amount of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.
Arvind.S vs Jagadeesh Chandra.

1 2.
Petitioner case is as Follows:

That on 15.02.2023 at about 23.00 P.M., the Petitioner was proceeding on a Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01/ET-2648 near Dommalur Water tank, old air port road,
Bangalore, wherein the driver of the water Tanker bearing Reg No.KA-02-1388 drove it with speed, rash and negligent manner, and dashed against to the two wheeler and caused the accident and thereby Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

He was shifted to Manipal hospital, wherein he took first aid, later he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, then he taken treatment in Aporva Hospital, as inpatient for the accidental injuries and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- for his treatment.
3. Petitioner stated that he is 28 years of age and he is working as coolie and thereby he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month,

Further he stated that the accident occurred due the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.27/2023 against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Petitioner alleged that the Respondent no.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and he insured his vehicle with respondent no.2 and accident caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and as such both are liable to pay the compensation with interest and he prayer this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, they appeared through their counsels files power and written statement.
They denied the entire version of the petitioner in toto.
Respondent No.1 contended that petitioner was alcoholic and accident occurred due to his negligent act.
Respondent No.2 admit the issuance policy to the vehicle of the respondent No.1 and contended that the insured has violated the policy conditions and they prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.

5. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and examined the medical record officers and doctor as PW.2 to 4, produced and marked 19 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 19 and they are fully cross examined.
6.
Respondent no.2 examined their official as RW-1 got marked two documents as Ex.D1 and 2 and he is fully cross examined.
7. I have heard the arguments from the counsel appearing for the petitioner.
Counsel appearing for respondent No.2 has filed the written arguments with an authority.
I have perused the same along with entire records.
7.1 Counsel appearing for respondent No.2 has relied on the following authorities:

1 . Rani & others Vs National Insurance Co.Ld and other - (2018) 8 SCC 492.
2.

D)- High court of Karnataka order dated 22.04.2022.

8. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following :
ISSUES 1.Whether the petitioner proves that, on 15.02.2023 at about 23.00 P.M., the Petitioner was proceeding on a Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01/ET-2648 near Dommalur Water tank, old air port road, Bangalore, wherein the driver of the water Tanker bearing Reg No.KA-02-1388 drove it with speed, rash and negligent manner,
and dashed against to the Petitioner's vehicle and caused the accident and thereby Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the said accident?
2 Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.What order or award?
Addl Issues on 28.07.2025:
1.
Whether respondent No.2 proves that insured has violated the policy conditions as contended in the written statement?
2.Whether the respondent No.1 proves that petitioner was consume the alcohol and accident occurred due to his negligent act as contended in the written statement?
I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, mahazar, sketch, IMV report, wound certificate, Final report, which are at Ex.P.1 to 7.
11.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents, it is evident that Rajesh Kannan was the driver of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident.

Mahazar, sketch, IMV report, final Arvind.S vs Jagadeesh Chandra.M on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136271200/
3 report establishes the involvement of the offending vehicle and the negligent act of the driver in the alleged accident.
12. In the cross-examination of PW-1, nothing worth has been elicited to disprove the petition allegation.
The alleged negligent act of the petitioner is not suggested to him.
Respondents have failed to establish their contention that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner and he was alcoholic as on the date of the accident.
In the cross examination of DW-1 he admit that they have issued the insurance policy to the vehicle belongs to respondent No.1 though the vehicle was not having valid permit.
It shows that respondent NO.1 has admitted its liability to the 3 rd party though there is no valid permit to the insured vehicle.
13. Admittedly petitioner has sustained grievous injury that is head injury/ bleeding in left anterior temporal lobe in the accident.

The final report which is at Ex.P7 is filed after investigation and it is the prima facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly the police records cannot be doubted and disbelieved as it has reached the finality.

14. Petitioner has tender the wound certificate, discharge summaries, inpatient record, mental status examination report as per Ex.P.6,8,14,13, the entry therein reveals that petitioner has sustained head injury and he has mild disability, connotative impairment with 19 scores, and he has taken treatment as inpatient for 7 days for the accidental injuries in the hospitals.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

15. Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization,
Medicines, Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
16.
Petitioner took treatment at NIMHANS & Apoorva hospital.

Evidently nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disbelieve the fact that he has sustained the head injuries and he has mild cog-native impairment in the alleged accident and he took treatment for the same.

Inasmuch,
discharge summaries, wound certificate and the medical reports issued form the hospitals has to be accepted.
Admittedly petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient for 7 days, he has incurred medical expenses of Rs.35,901/- as per Ex.P.10.

Further for the attendant charges, transportation,
nourishing food, he might have spend some more expenses.
Therefore I award Rs.20,000/-, in total petitioner is entitled for Rs.55,901/- under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period.
17. The petitioner has not substantiated his nature of work and income as alleged in the petition.
Accident took place on 2023 however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2023 is Rs.16,000/-, and same is assessed and considered as his monthly income.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that petitioner has lost the income.
Therefore I award Rs.16,000/- as compensation under this head.
Arvind.S vs Jagadeesh Chandra.

M on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136271200/
4
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
18. The petitioner has examined the Neuro surgeon Dr.Shreedhar as PW-4.

He deposed that, as per the neuro psychological assessment report of the petitioner given by Dr.Arpitha and by clinical examination of the petitioner that, petitioner has mild disability, cognitive impairment of less than 40% and whole body disability is 20% as per Ex.17 to 19.
He deposed that Dr.Arpitha examined the petitioner in his presence.
He deposed that some clotted blood crystals is still there in the brain membrine and petitioner is having irritation the restlessness as stated in the discharge summary which is at Ex.P.8.
He deposed that petitioner has not recovered even after taking treatment for 6 months, he deposed that brain stem and ventricular of the petitioner is not affected.
He deposed that petitioner can perform his daily routine work and head injury has affected petitioner memory.
He admitted that petitioner has undergone rehabilitation.
I have perused the testimony of PW-1, 4 and wound certificate, discharge summaries given by the hospitals, Mental status report, inpatient records.
19. Evidently petitioner has not examined the doctors who has treated him in the hospitals.
It is true that petitioner sustained the grievous head injury that is bleeding in left anterior temporal lobe and he has nuero psychological mind cognitive disability.

Petitioner has lost his thinking capacity,
memory and he is facing difficulty in finding the words and suffering with forgetfulness.
No doubt the aforesaid impediment troubles the petitioner during his life time.
Considering the medical reports and oral testimony of doctor, the whole body disability of the petitioner is assessed as 18.5%.

20. The notional monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.16,000/-, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident is 28 years as per his affidavit and medical record and it is not disputed by the respondent No.2.
The multiplier applicable to this case is "17".

Therefore loss of income on account of permanent disability is calculated as follows;
Rs.16,000/-(Monthly income)X12(Months)X 17(Multiplier) X18.5% (Disability) = Rs.6,03,840/-.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.6,03,840 /- as compensation under this head.
Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
21.
It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained grievous head injury.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, he might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings and due to accidental injuries.
There fore I award Rs.30,000/- under these conventional heads.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
22.

The petitioner has to forego certain amenities available for him due to the accidental injuries,
therefore I award Rs.30,000/- as compensation under this head.
23. Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.

In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

 1 Towards attendant charges, Rs. 55,901/-
 transportation, nourishing food  2 Loss of income during the laid up period Rs. 16,000/-
 3 Loss of income on account of Rs.6,03,840/-
 permanent disability  4 pain & sufferings Rs. 30,000/-
 5 loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/-
24. Rate of Interest:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s
Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
25. Liability:

The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, they have failed to established its defence that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner.
In the cross examination of DW-1, he clearly admitted that they have issued the policy coverage to the vehicle belongs to respondent No.1 though the vehicle was not having valid permit.
The said fact establishes that the insurer has accepted the aforesaid risk factor.
Accordingly authority at Sl No.2, 3 at para 7.1 relied on by the respondent No.2 cannot be made applicable to the present case, in view of the substantial oral testimony of DW-1.

As such respondent No.2 is the liable to pay the compensation amount with interest, respondent No.2 is directed to deposit compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

Hence with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record, Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1 the affirmative, Additional Issue No.1 & 2 in the negative, issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
26. Issue No.3:
For the foregoing reason and discussion, on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.7,35,741/-with interest at the rate of 6% P.A from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Respondent no.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, Cash sheristedar is directed to release the entire amount to the petitioner through K2, after compliance of mandate of circular No.39/2020 dated 17.01.2020.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
